_meta.slot_divergences: T5 PREDATES THE SLOT SCHEMA. Tekken 5 (PS2, 2004) introduced character customization, but its data does NOT use the T6 4-slot / T7 16-slot item-slot system: in TK5DATA1.BIN each character pack (19-entry archive) carries exactly ONE costume model (sub02, full body incl. head/hair/props as a single NUDP) + ONE low-poly full-body model (sub05) + TIM2 textures (sub01). NO per-slot item meshes (no separate HEAD/UPPER/LOWER/HAIR_ACC NUDP entries) exist in any of the 80 packs — verified by full NUDP census (464 occurrences classified) and own-eyes renders. Per-slot item data, if present in this build at all, can only live in (a) the 9 ctype-5 containers whose models use the undecoded VIF 0x82 vertex format, or (b) TK5DATA0.BIN, which remains encrypted under a second cipher layer and is the suspected home of the content for DATA1's 216 empty table slots. Mapping T5 content onto the registry shape therefore happens at FULL_BODY (whole-costume) granularity at conversion time, and any finer slot claim would be invented — it is NOT made here.
_meta.status: SURVEYED — SOURCE DATA EXTRACTED AND CHECKSUM-VERIFIED; NO SLOT PARTS CONVERTED YET. parts[] is empty for the same reason Tekken 7's catalog shipped empty in PR #437 (meshes not yet in converted holdings), with one difference: T5's disc data IS now extracted (1,355 files, 0 checksum failures) and the costume-pack census is complete, so the gaps below are conversion/format gaps and one encryption gap — each with its exact unblock route in the survey doc. named_gaps[] is documentation only — it is NOT part of parts[], the runtime never resolves it, and resolveProfileParts() reports a named-gap part_id as 'unresolved' until the real part lands in parts[].
_meta.suite_slot_mapping: T5 content -> suite_slot (at conversion time): whole-costume model (pack sub02) -> full_body; low-poly body (pack sub05) -> full_body (LOD variant, not a separate part); ctype-5 container models (VIF 0x82, undecoded) -> slot assigned from decoded geometry at conversion time, never before. T7 slot names are used in by_slot purely as the shared registry shape (all zero today).

named_gaps.acquisition: Decode the VIF 0x82 vertex layout (working models use globalFlags 0x91/0x93; every ctype-5 model uses 0x82 and ModelMagic's VIFerator desyncs on all of them). Byte-budget solve per submesh (vertCount is in the VIF header) or Ghidra trace of the renderer path. THEN render and classify by geometry. Files: DATA1 0022 (system), 0687/0698, 0753/0764, 1061/1072/1083/1094 (per-group twins).
named_gaps.expected_source: 9 ctype-5 containers in TK5DATA1.BIN: [u32 count=5][subs: TIM2 set, NUDP set (VIF globalFlags 0x82), MIF, small data, data]. 16 NUDP models total (1,520-19,264 B). Header metadata only until the format decodes — geometry deliberately NOT characterized in this catalog (a coordinator cross-check flagged that a 'head portrait' characterization of the 1061 pair was another lane's T6 finding, not T5 evidence).

named_gaps.acquisition: Teardown-lane cipher work (owner NO-DEFERRAL teardown program): TK5-DATA0-CIPHER-HUNT.md + this lane's new head evidence (survey S6): DATA0's first bytes XOR with an LCG keystream whose seed at word 0 is 1; words 5-11 of the raw file ARE the keystream (plaintext zeros); block-restart seed-1 decryption yields a structured head (word2=0x4400) then a second periodic layer — the transform is NOT the DATA1 scheme alone. PCSX2 runtime extraction (cipher-hunt S8) is the documented fallback that settles it.

DATA1's table holds 216 records with size 0xFFFFFFFF (empty) — including two slots (+7/+8) in most character groups — whose content is not in DATA1; DATA0 is the only other character-data archive on the disc.
